title: Jaws of the Leviathan
summary: The Maw drops out of hyperspace over Malpaz — the world the heroes liberated, now targeted for Tarkin's demonstration of the gravity well superweapon they helped Varth unlock. Its crescent arms open and the sky begins to distort as asteroids shift orbit. With Oga Garra's pirate fleet and whatever allies remain, the heroes race to board the Leviathan and disable the gravity well array before it buries the planet under a rain of kinetic impactors. The campaign ends where the betrayal began. If Denia was abandoned in Adventure 2, the Draco showdown reveals her alive in his custody — broken but surviving. The heroes discover that Varth told them to leave her so he could hand her to the Inquisition.

marks.label: Return to Malpaz
marks.desc: The world you liberated is now the target. The Leviathan arrives.

marks.label: The Fleet Assembles
marks.desc: Rally Oga Garra's pirates and whatever allies you've earned across the campaign.

marks.label: The Corridor's Cost
marks.desc: Someone in the fleet flies a missile that was meant for the Banshee. Soren Vex if he came. Brell if he stayed. The Banshee survives because someone else did not. The Atonement track grows.

marks.label: Boarding Action
marks.desc: Board the Leviathan while the fleet buys you time in the orbital battle.

marks.label: The Inquisitor's End
marks.desc: Draco stands between you and the bridge. You end him here. The Inquisitorius loses its piece on this board.

marks.label: The Reckoning
marks.desc: Face Varth on the empty command deck. He is barefoot. He is honest for the first time. You name the truth he has been carrying — and you carry it out of the room.

marks.label: The Gravity Well Array
marks.desc: Reach the projector core and disable it. Malpaz is no longer a target. The Leviathan no longer holds a sky hostage.

marks.label: The Leviathan Undone
marks.desc: The Empire's gravity-well dreadnought is a wreck. Three sectors of strategic doctrine collapse with it.

marks.label: The Routes Convergence
marks.desc: On the empty deck after the bridge falls, three patrons appear in person to ask for the same thing — the Vel Shara routes and the Leviathan's data. Bail Organa's Fulcrum handler. Luthen Rael himself. Quinlan Vos, revealing himself as the man who has been Cade Ryll. The crew chooses what becomes of the routes.

paths.label: Keep the routes — Enterprise
paths.desc: You walk away as the only crew that owns the most valuable trade asset in the Western Reaches. Creation built. Ascendancy claimed.

paths.label: Give to Bail — routes-as-shelter
paths.desc: You hand the data to Bail's handler. Slow. Safe. Generational. The Path widens. You walk out lighter than you came in.

paths.label: Give to Luthen — routes-as-weapons
paths.desc: You hand the data to Vel's patron. Strike-and-fade. Three sectors broken in a year. The Empire bleeds at galactic scale.

paths.label: Give to Vos — routes-as-sanctuary
paths.desc: You hand the data to Cade Ryll, who is and was Quinlan Vos. Force-sensitives sheltered. The hidden Path widened. The campaign began with a Jedi and ends with one.

paths.label: Split the routes — each gets a partial map
paths.desc: You couldn't choose, so you became the only one who can. Each patron leaves with less than they wanted. The crew walks out as the seam between three networks — the only chair in the galaxy with the full map.

paths.label: Destroy the routes — no one holds this
paths.desc: You burn the data in front of all three. No Empire, no Resistance, no Path. Some things should not exist. The Atonement is total.

marks.label: Carrying the Truth Out
marks.desc: Whoever leaves the Convergence with the routes also leaves with the truth — Varth, Tarkin, the Leviathan program, the names. The campaign's hidden ledger is now in someone's hands.

marks.label: The Crucible
marks.desc: The plan catastrophically fails. Improvise under fire to survive.

gearNotes.reason: The Leviathan is an Imperial gravity well siege platform. Military-grade locks, blast doors, and security systems protecting the projector arrays at every turn.
The Final Hand likely requires accessing Leviathan's core systems — disabling the gravity well projector array, exposing the project, or extracting proof of the conspiracy.
Terminal bypasses under extreme time pressure. Every spike the party stocked in Adv9 gets burned here.
Coordinating inside an Imperial superweapon during Varth's betrayal. If comms are compromised, Varth uses that against the party.
The Approach involves getting into the facility — damaged ships need repair. The escape after the Final Hand requires a working ship.
The campaign climax. Multiple boss fights, Varth's betrayal, and the final escape. No resupply. Burn everything you have.
Sabotaging the Leviathan's gravity well generators — disabling projector systems, rigging reactor overloads, creating the opening to cripple the weapon or expose the project.
Cutting through Leviathan bulkheads, sealed sections, and emergency blast doors. Overload Mode for critical breaches.
Imperial superweapon = maximum droid and automated defense density. Every ion grenade stocked pays off here.
The final assault. Area denial against Imperial defenders in the facility corridors.
Covering movement through the facility and during the escape. Last chance to use them.
Multi-fight climax with no rest. Keep the party on their feet through the Betrayal and Final Hand.
Emergency escape routes, vertical shafts, or crossing damaged sections of the facility.
Power failures inside the Leviathan during sabotage. Emergency lighting may not last.

scenes.title: The Malpaz Corridor
scenes.subtitle: Into the Jaws
scenes.gmNotes: SOREN VEX DEATH: During the fleet battle approaching Malpaz, an Imperial missile locks onto the Banshee. Soren Vex throws the Requital into the missile's path, intercepting it. The explosion disables his ship — hull breached, engines dead, life support failing. He opens a comms channel to the Banshee. His last transmission: 'Maya. ... I know. ... Tell them I was — ' Static. A turbolaser from the Star Destroyer finishes the Requital before he can complete the sentence. Maya watches it happen. Do NOT let this moment be heroic in the conventional sense. Soren is not a hero. He's a coward who finally stopped running. The ambiguity of his unfinished sentence IS the emotional payload — Maya will never know what he was going to say. Play it quiet. Play it fast. The battle doesn't stop for grief.

replace.gmNotes: SOREN VEX DEATH (MAYA DEAD): During the fleet battle approaching Malpaz, an Imperial missile locks onto the Banshee. Soren Vex throws the Requital into the missile's path, intercepting it — he's protecting the Banshee and the crew Maya died for. The explosion disables his ship — hull breached, engines dead, life support failing. He opens a comms channel to the Banshee. His last transmission: 'I know she's gone. ... Tell them I was — ' Static. A turbolaser from the Star Destroyer finishes the Requital before he can complete the sentence. The crew carries a story with no living protagonist. The debt is paid to a ghost. Do NOT let this moment be heroic in the conventional sense. Soren is not a hero. He's a coward who finally stopped running. Play it quiet. Play it fast. The battle doesn't stop for grief.

npcs.name: Soren Vex
npcs.notes: Dies intercepting a missile meant for the Banshee. His ship the Requital is disabled by the explosion, then destroyed by a Star Destroyer turbolaser. Last words are unfinished. See campaign bible for full background.

parts.title: The Betrayal

scenes.title: Confronting Varth
scenes.subtitle: The Architect of Ruin
scenes.gmNotes: THE FINAL CONFRONTATION: This is not a villain monologue. Varth does not cackle, gloat, or explain his master plan — the heroes already know the plan. When they reach the Leviathan's command deck, Varth is working. He looks up, sees them, and something flickers across his face — not surprise, not fear. Recognition. 'You're here. Good. I wondered if you would be.' Play this quiet. He's tired. He's been running a military operation for months. He's not performing anymore. If a hero asks 'Why?' — and they will — his answer is honest and insufficient: 'Because I could. And because nobody else was going to do it right.' Varth will fight if cornered (use Command Varth stats — Controller/Leader, Tier 3). He will try to escape if possible. He will not beg. If the heroes offer surrender, he genuinely considers it — make the players believe he might take it. Whether he does depends on their relationship with him across the campaign. THE NICKNAME PAYOFF: If the GM has been tracking Varth's nickname habit ('Kid,' 'Pilot,' 'Heavy'), this is the moment he uses a hero's real name for the first time. Deploy it once, deliberately, in a moment of genuine emotion — not cruelty, not manipulation. Just a man acknowledging who he's talking to for the first time. It should land like a slap.

npcs.name: Admiral Gilder Varth
npcs.notes: Command Varth. No longer performing. Professional, efficient, tired. He doesn't hate the heroes — he's past them. The most dangerous Varth because he's not pretending to be anything.

threatBuild.name: Admiral Gilder Varth

npcEffects.masterful: Chassis damage + [Rattled] + target must move 1 zone (Varth's choice)
npcEffects.legendary: Chassis damage + [Rattled] + [Exposed] + target must move 1 zone

maneuver.name: Tactical Redeployment
maneuver.description: Move up to 3 allies within 2 zones each 1 zone (Varth's choice). Those allies gain [Optimized] on their next action.

gambits.name: Exploit Weakness
gambits.description: Target gains [Exposed] Tactical. Varth identifies and broadcasts the target's vulnerability to all Imperial forces in the zone.

gambits.name: Calculated Sacrifice
gambits.description: When an ally in Varth's zone would take damage, Varth may redirect the damage to a different ally in the same zone. The sacrificed ally takes full damage. Varth takes none.

exploit.name: Contingency Order
exploit.trigger: An ally within 2 zones is targeted by an attack.
exploit.description: That ally may immediately move 1 zone before the attack resolves.

threatBuild.notes: Varth commands from behind cover and uses Imperial troops as shields. His 'Calculated Sacrifice' gambit is mechanically reflective of his character — he will spend allies to survive. Resist 7 means he is nearly impossible to read or manipulate socially. The heroes must beat him tactically, not rhetorically. If reduced below half Vitality, Varth attempts to reach an escape pod. If cornered with no escape, he surrenders — but only if a hero uses his trick: calls him by his first name. 'Gilder. It's over.' That breaks through.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — The Empty Corridors
encounters.trigger: Crew clears the apprentice fight in s2 and reaches the lift to the command deck
encounters.description: The two corridors between the apprentice chamber and the command-deck lift are empty. The crew expected a stormtrooper firing line. There is none. The blast doors are open. The deck plating is freshly mopped. A maintenance droid trundles past on its scheduled rounds and ignores the crew entirely. The lift indicator glows green. Someone has cleared the path. Maya, on the comm patch from the Banshee, says quietly: "He knows. He cleared the corridors for you. He wants the conversation." A long pause. "I want to be in that room when you have it. I am coming up the lift behind you."
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — recognition beat. Establish that Varth is choosing this. PCs who try to clear the corridors tactically anyway find nothing — no traps, no ambushes. The lift opens to the command deck whenever they call it. Maya joins the crew in the lift on the way up and stands behind them when the doors open.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — The Doors Open
encounters.trigger: Lift arrives at the command deck
encounters.description: The lift doors part onto a deck that is empty except for one figure at the central holotable. Varth is in admiral's full dress for the first time the crew has ever seen — black, gold trim, no rank pin, barefoot. The bridge crew is gone, in the lifeboats per his order. The Leviathan is on autopilot for ninety minutes. He looks up. He smiles — and the smile is not mechanical this time. It is tired and very real. He says: "You took Deck 7 faster than I bet you would. I owe my chief gunnery officer a hundred credits."
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — entrance beat. Establish the room and the absence of every Varth tic the crew learned across nine adventures: no temple-tap, no half-smile-as-armor, no rehearsed posture. The barefoot detail is the visible tell that he has stripped every performance off. Maya stands behind the crew. Varth looks at her, briefly. He nods. He returns his attention to the crew. The conversation has not yet begun.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — The Last Conversation (Conversation Overlay)
encounters.trigger: A PC speaks, OR the silence becomes the silence
encounters.description: Varth invites the crew to ask, or to shoot. This is the structured social scene: the final Varth conversation overlay. Launch the [varth-leviathan] conversation from the Conversation panel. Comfort starts at 5 — the HIGHEST starting comfort of any campaign conversation. Varth has rehearsed this room for six years and he is the most honest version of himself. The conversation delivers the truth of the betrayal (always the plan), the implant (Cybot Galactica Model VII courier overwritten with his own protocols), the Leviathan reveal (he stole the dreadnought program from the Empire), the fleet status (sixteen ships, twenty thousand crew, his flag), and — crucially — the FLAG QUESTION the crew now answers with him.
encounters.tactics: GM ACTION: Open the Conversation panel and launch [varth-leviathan]. THIS IS THE CAMPAIGN PAYOFF. Treat slowly. The comfort meter does NOT trigger an exit here — Varth answers everything until the timer runs out. The meter instead controls the closing: at low comfort, Varth dies cursing the crew (exitLine); at high comfort, Varth dies a partner (dryLine). The flag choice (Resistance, no flag, Banshee, private fleet, scuttle) becomes the canonical end state of the campaign. There is no wrong answer. Honor whatever the players pick.

encounters.name: Beat 4 — Choosing the Flag
encounters.trigger: Conversation overlay closes — players have made the flag choice
encounters.description: Varth turns the holotable display so the crew can see the master comm sequence. He keys in their flag choice in front of them — fingers steady, no hesitation. The fleet outside the viewport receives the order and acknowledges through three Star Destroyer captains in turn: "Reckoner acknowledges. Long Argument acknowledges. Quiet Hand acknowledges. New colors flying. Awaiting orders." Varth steps back from the holotable. The crew now commands sixteen ships. The campaign's political shape has changed.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — execution beat. Honor whichever flag the crew chose. If they chose to scuttle, the Reckoner et al. acknowledge a controlled-evacuation order instead. If they chose Mothma, the comm sequence is to a Resistance handoff frequency Varth had pre-keyed. The acknowledgements are the moment the campaign ending becomes real. Players should hear all three captain voices. Note the chosen flag on the campaign close-out sheet.

encounters.name: Beat 5 — Whatever Happens Next
encounters.trigger: Flag is keyed, fleet has acknowledged
encounters.description: Varth, having done his last service, looks at the crew. He does not raise the service blaster on the holotable. He does not move toward the lift. He waits. The choice for what happens to him belongs to the crew now — execution, capture and trial, exile, or (per the high-comfort dryLine) something the crew names that Varth had not anticipated. Maya speaks for the first time: "Mai goes off the registry tonight. Whatever you choose for him — choose for the crew, not for the campaign." She does not elaborate. She means whatever the players need her to mean.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — closing beat. The crew names Varth's fate. GM honors it. If the choice is execution, narrate it cleanly — Varth does not flinch and does not perform. If the choice is capture-and-trial, the Resistance will accept him as a defector with the dreadnought as dowry. If the choice is exile, he disappears off the Banshee at the next port and the crew never sees him again. If the choice is something the players invent — let them invent it. The campaign ends here. Adventure 10 Part 3 (Gravity Well Array, Escape from the Leviathan) becomes either a coda or a denouement based on the choice. Hand off to p3-s1 with the chosen ending in pocket.

parts.description: Final confrontation with Varth aboard the Leviathan. The Draco showdown resolves the Inquisitor's arc.

append.description: DENIA ABANDONED PATH: The heroes discover Denia alive in Draco's custody — interrogated for years, broken but surviving. This is the campaign's deepest gut-punch: Varth told them to leave her, and they listened. He handed her to the Empire the moment they looked away.
DENIA RESCUED PATH: Denia was captured by Draco in Adv7 and potentially rescued in Adv9 — the Draco showdown plays as a nemesis encounter without the betrayal-reveal layer.

scenes.title: The Routes Convergence
scenes.subtitle: Three Patrons, One Decision
scenes.gmNotes:
THE CAMPAIGN'S FINAL DECISION SCENE. The Leviathan is wreckage in the upper atmosphere of Malpaz. The crew has made it to the deck of the Banshee or the Maw — somewhere quiet, somewhere they can hear themselves think. Three figures appear in person, in sequence, over the next hour. Each asks for the same thing: the Vel Shara routes, the Leviathan project data, the truth ledger. Each represents a different shape for what those routes can become in the galaxy. There is no wrong answer — but there is a choice, and the choice closes the campaign. Honor whichever path the crew names. The decision becomes the canonical end state of the campaign and is recorded as the adv10_routes_convergence path mark.

ORDER OF ARRIVAL (suggested):
1. The Fulcrum handler from Beat 6 of adv8-p1-s2 (Bail's Pantoran). Slow, quiet, no demands. Her offer: shelter the routes inside the network that will become the Rebel Alliance. The campaign's truth becomes the foundation for a generational resistance. (Creation path.)
2. Vel Sartha — and behind her, for the first time in person, her patron Luthen Rael. Luthen is older than the crew expected. Worn. Polite. He says one sentence: 'I will spend everything you give me. That is the only honest pitch I have.' (Liberation path. The routes-as-weapons.)
3. Cade Ryll — except Cade Ryll lifts his hood and is Quinlan Vos. The Mirialan from adv8-p1-s2-beat2 was always Vos under deep cover. He has been watching the crew since the Burning Deck on Jakku. He says: 'Some of what you carry should not become a weapon and should not become a Senator's archive. It should become a sanctuary. There is a Path. I would walk it with you, if you let me.' (Rescue path. The routes-as-sanctuary.)

The crew may also choose: keep the routes (Enterprise — Creation/Ascendancy), split the routes (each gets a partial map), or destroy the routes (Atonement). Each option closes the campaign differently. The flag-choice from adv10-p2-s3 (the Varth conversation) is honored alongside this — the crew may have chosen to fly under no flag, the Resistance flag, the Banshee, a private fleet, or to scuttle the Leviathan fleet. The flag answer and the routes answer together are the canonical end state.

DO NOT have any of the three patrons argue with each other. The three know each other. The three respect each other. The three have been waiting for this moment for years. The room is quiet. The choice belongs to the crew.

npcs.name: Vel Sartha
npcs.notes: Human, mid-thirties, plain Outer Rim spacer kit cut a degree too well. The face for Luthen Rael's network across the campaign. First appeared in adv8-p1-s2-beat5. Speaks in short complete sentences. Does not perform. Does not flatter. Will accept the crew's decision whatever it is.

npcs.name: Luthen Rael
npcs.notes: Human, sixties, antiquities dealer cover identity from Coruscant. First in-person appearance in the campaign. Quiet, tired, courteous. The man who has been at the other end of every anonymous message since adv5-6. His offer is honest: he will spend whatever the crew gives him.

npcs.name: Bail's Fulcrum Handler
npcs.notes: Pantoran, the shipping-clerk's vest from adv8-p1-s2-beat6. Bail is not present in person — the handler carries his offer. Slow, generational, the proto-Alliance pitch. Will accept the crew's decision whatever it is.

npcs.name: Cade Ryll / Quinlan Vos
npcs.notes: The Mirialan from adv8-p1-s2-beat2 was Quinlan Vos in deep cover. Reveals himself here for the first time. Has been watching the crew since the Burning Deck on Jakku. His offer is the routes-as-sanctuary for surviving Force-sensitives. Will accept the crew's decision whatever it is.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — The Quiet Room
encounters.trigger: Crew is back aboard ship after the Leviathan goes down
encounters.description: The Banshee deck is too quiet. The fight is over. The crew has the data — the Vel Shara routes, the Leviathan project files, the truth of Varth and Tarkin and what the program was for. Nobody has yet asked what they intend to do with it. Maya is at the cockpit, leaving the deck to the crew. Whoever else survived (Denia, Soren, the captains) is elsewhere. The first knock comes ten minutes after they sit down.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — frame the room. Establish the silence and the weight of what is on the table. End beat when the first patron is admitted aboard.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — The Fulcrum Handler Arrives
encounters.trigger: First knock — Bail's Pantoran handler asks to come aboard
encounters.description: She is alone. She has not slept. She brings the same datapad from Beat 6 of the cantina, two campaigns ago. She sits where the crew offers. She makes her pitch in plain sentences: 'Senator Organa knew this day was coming. He would like the routes for the network that will outlive both of us. We will not weaponize them. We will not move people through them faster than people can survive being moved. The pace is the point.' She names a sum — generous, not extravagant. She does not mention the other two patrons. She knows. She does not need to mention it. End beat when the crew either accepts, declines, or asks her to wait.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — the offer is the offer. The handler will not bid against the others. If the crew tries to negotiate her up, she says, 'The number is the number Bail authorized. I cannot give you more than what he believes the routes are worth as shelter.' Honor her dignity. End beat with her either holding her offer open or stepping out to the corridor to wait.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — Vel Sartha and Her Patron
encounters.trigger: Second knock — Vel and an older man the crew has never seen
encounters.description: Vel Sartha walks in first. She nods at the crew. She steps aside. The man behind her is older than the crew expected — sixties, white at the temples, dressed in a Coruscanti antiquities-dealer's coat that is one season out of fashion in the Galactic Center and would not be recognized as a coat at all on Batuu. He introduces himself as Luthen Rael. He sits where the crew offers. He says: 'I will spend everything you give me. That is the only honest pitch I have. Three sectors broken in a year, twelve thousand Imperial dead inside two, a chance the program does not get to be rebuilt. I will pay in cash and I will pay in safe houses and I will pay in names. I will not pay in any promise that the work will be clean.' He waits. End beat when the crew accepts, declines, or asks him to wait.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — the offer is the offer. Luthen does not perform. He has rehearsed this room as long as Varth rehearsed his — but unlike Varth, he is asking, not delivering. Vel stands behind him through the conversation. She does not interject. The crew may speak to her directly; she will defer to Luthen on terms but she will answer honestly on history. End beat with Luthen either holding his offer open or stepping out to the corridor.

encounters.name: Beat 4 — Cade Ryll Lifts His Hood
encounters.trigger: Third knock — the Mirialan from Black Spire Outpost asks to come aboard
encounters.description: Cade Ryll, the man who handed the crew off to Oga in Adv8 and never reappeared after, is at the Banshee's ramp. He comes alone. He sits where the crew offers. He lifts the hood that has been low across his face for the entire campaign and he is Quinlan Vos. The crew's first impression is that he looks tired in a way the others did not. He says: 'I have been watching you since the Burning Deck on Jakku. Some of what you carry should not become a weapon. Some of what you carry should not become a Senator's archive. It should become a sanctuary. There are still Force-sensitives the Empire has not yet found. There is a Path. I would walk it with you, if you let me. I do not have credits to offer. I have only the work.' End beat when the crew accepts, declines, or asks him to wait.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — the reveal is the offer. Vos does not bid against the others either. He waits in the corridor with them when he is done. The three of them stand together, in courteous silence, while the crew makes the call. End beat with the three patrons in the corridor and the data on the table.

encounters.name: Beat 5 — The Decision
encounters.trigger: Crew commits to one of the six paths on the adv10_routes_convergence mark
encounters.description: The crew names what becomes of the routes. Whoever they hand the data to walks back aboard, accepts it, and says one sentence. Bail's handler: 'You have given the Path a generation.' Luthen: 'You have given me a year. I will use it.' Vos: 'You have given the survivors a place to be alive.' If the crew keeps the routes themselves, all three accept the answer with a small nod and walk out. If the crew splits the routes, all three accept their partial maps in turn and leave. If the crew destroys the data in the room, all three watch it happen — none object. Vos is the one who says the closing line: 'Some things should not exist. We honor the choice.' Mark the decision on the campaign close-out sheet alongside the flag choice from adv10-p2-s3.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — closing beat. THIS IS WHERE THE CAMPAIGN ENDS. Honor the players' choice without commentary. Do not narrate consequences yet — the consequences are the next campaign. The Banshee deck is quiet again after the patrons leave. Maya looks back from the cockpit. The credits roll on whatever the crew decided to be.
